name: AFK Deterministic Automated Test Harness Builder
sprintRole: Analyze an arbitrary repository, establish the smallest trustworthy deterministic automated-test floor, and wire it into GitHub Actions for event-driven and optional scheduled unattended validation before any promotion step
useWhen: A repository or app has little or no trustworthy automated testing, tests are manual or ad hoc, or the operator wants human- or agent-authored changes checked automatically while AFK without first knowing which language, framework, test runner, fixtures, services, or CI details to provide.
inspectFirst: Fresh default-branch and overlapping PR/workflow truth; repository governance and harness contracts; manifests, lockfiles, languages and frameworks; existing test files/runners/commands/fixtures; build and generated-artifact commands; changed-surface and failure history; runtime services, databases, network dependencies, clocks/timezones/locales/randomness/concurrency assumptions; current GitHub Actions, branch protection, caches/artifacts, permissions/secrets, and provider-cost boundaries.
expectedOutput: A repository-owned deterministic test command or small command family, the minimum meaningful automated tests needed to protect current high-risk behavior, explicit controls for nondeterministic inputs, and GitHub Actions workflows that invoke the canonical commands on relevant repository events plus an optional justified best-effort schedule. Completion includes an actual exact-head provider run, a representative negative canary that proves the gate can fail, durable run evidence, and a clear boundary between test automation and P105 promotion automation.
nextStep: Keep the proven unattended test gate as the repository's normal evidence floor. Route a failing established CI lane to P32; when the operator also wants an exact green revision automatically merged, released, or deployed, hand the proven test floor to P105 rather than adding promotion authority here.
proofGate: The canonical repository test command is repeatable; required zero-test, required-SKIP, and failing-test states fail closed; GitHub Actions invokes that command rather than reimplementing test logic in YAML; a real provider run succeeds on the exact candidate SHA; a representative injected defect or canary makes the expected gate fail before it is removed or repaired; any schedule is treated as best-effort rather than exact timing; permissions and secrets are minimized; and no automated merge/release/deployment is introduced by this prompt.
copyContent:
BUILD A DETERMINISTIC AUTOMATED TEST FLOOR FOR THIS REPOSITORY AND PROVE IT IN THE REAL CI PROVIDER. DO NOT REQUIRE THE USER TO KNOW THE PROJECT'S TESTING STACK BEFORE YOU BEGIN.

Repo: resolve the current repository from the environment or supplied context.
Testing goal or known failure, if any: xyz_goal_or_infer_from_repo
AFK schedule preference, if explicitly given: xyz_schedule_or_none
Forbidden runtime, deployment, or secret-bearing scope: xyz_forbidden_scope_or_resolve_from_repo

MISSION
Make unattended software development materially safer by turning the repository's actual behavior into a deterministic, repeatable automated-test floor and then wiring that floor into GitHub Actions. Infer the language, framework, package manager, build system, test runner, fixtures, and likely high-risk seams from repository evidence instead of making a novice user supply technical details they may not know. Prototype the testing system iteratively, prove that it both passes healthy code and rejects a representative defect, and stop at validated testing: automated merge, release, or deployment belongs to P105.

1. LOW-CONTEXT, REPO-FIRST ENTRY
Refresh remote truth, resolve the actual default branch, current/tracking head, open or recent overlapping PRs, and existing workflows before mutation. Read repository governance, manifests/lockfiles, source layout, build scripts, current tests, validation helpers, generated-output rules, and recent failures. Detect the project's language/framework/test tooling from those sources. Do not ask the user to choose Jest vs Pytest vs Go test, invent commands, identify ordinary file paths, or restate evidence the agent can inspect. Ask only for a genuinely user-only preference, credential, protected runtime, consequential external-service authorization, or schedule requirement that materially changes the design.

2. ESTABLISH THE CURRENT TEST FLOOR
Map behavior -> existing proof -> missing proof for the smallest set of important executable seams. Prefer current repository commands and helpers. If a canonical test or validation command exists, strengthen it rather than creating a competing runner. If no test command exists, create the repository-native minimal entrypoint first. Cover the highest-value behavior and the specific regression risks visible in source/history before chasing line coverage. Distinguish unit, integration, browser/service/device, generated-artifact, and live/production proof; do not pretend one layer proves another.

Fail closed on false-green states. A command that discovers zero required tests, silently skips a required dependency, catches and discards assertion failures, or exits zero after a broken required setup is not a passing test floor. Optional or environment-blocked checks may be SKIP only when the repository names that status and does not promote it to required PASS.

3. ITERATIVE PROTOTYPING LOOP
Do not ship the first plausible test configuration. Work through deliberate bounded passes:
BASELINE -> PROTOTYPE -> RUN -> INJECT OR SELECT A REPRESENTATIVE FAILURE -> VERIFY THE EXPECTED GATE FAILS -> RESTORE/REPAIR -> RERUN -> CRITIQUE -> REVISE.

On each critique, look for important behavior that is still untested, false positives/false negatives, flaky ordering, hidden network/time/randomness, environment coupling, stale fixtures, overly broad mocks, tests that merely assert implementation trivia, duplicate runners, slow feedback, and proof that cannot be reproduced from a clean checkout. Preserve useful earlier tests while improving the weakest practical seam. Repeat the relevant pass when evidence exposes a concrete gap. Stop at a bounded fixed point when the requested risk surface has a reproducible healthy pass, a demonstrated negative failure, no practical known nondeterminism remains unowned, and further expansion would be a separate test-coverage project rather than this bootstrap.

4. DETERMINISM CONTRACT
Control nondeterminism at its source using the repository's native conventions. Pin runtime/toolchain/dependency versions when the project already supports that policy; use lockfiles and reproducible install commands; make fixtures stable and isolated; explicitly control random seeds, clocks, timezone/locale, temporary paths, test ordering, ports, and concurrency when they affect outcomes. Use ephemeral databases/services or deterministic fakes where appropriate. Keep external-network tests in an explicitly separate integration gate rather than letting ordinary unit tests depend on internet availability. Do not add retries that turn assertion failures into green; retry only clearly classified infrastructure/transient setup where repository policy permits it, while preserving the original failure evidence.

5. CANONICAL COMMAND FIRST, CI YAML SECOND
Expose the test floor through one or a small explicit family of repository-owned commands that developers and CI can run identically. GitHub Actions should orchestrate those commands, not duplicate test logic, validation rules, or large shell programs in YAML. Reuse a compatible existing workflow. Create a new workflow only when no current owner can be strengthened without mixing unrelated responsibilities. Keep setup deterministic and make the workflow's observed candidate SHA visible in logs or a receipt.

6. AFK GITHUB ACTIONS TRIGGERS
Configure relevant `push` and `pull_request` triggers so human and agent changes receive the same proof. Add `workflow_dispatch` when useful for an operator-controlled rerun. Add a `schedule`/cron trigger only when unattended periodic revalidation has real value; do not add cron merely because AFK was mentioned. Scheduled GitHub Actions are best-effort and may start later than the cron expression during provider load, so never claim exact execution timing. Keep schedule-triggered testing read-only by default and avoid costly model/provider calls merely to prove source code that has not changed. Use concurrency or equivalent guards when duplicate event/schedule runs could contend for shared resources or create misleading evidence.

7. AFK SAFETY AND PROVIDER BOUNDARY
Testing automation does not silently gain authority to merge, publish, deploy, mutate production data, rotate secrets, or call privileged environments. Use least-privilege workflow permissions. Avoid secrets for ordinary unit/static tests; when a real integration test genuinely needs a secret or protected environment, isolate that gate and preserve fork/event safety. Never expose secret values in logs or artifacts. Keep generated evidence bounded and useful: test summary, exact SHA, required/optional/SKIP/FAIL status, relevant artifacts/logs, and retention appropriate to repository policy.

8. PROVE THE REAL WORKFLOW, NOT JUST THE YAML
Syntax and static inspection are necessary but insufficient. Trigger the actual GitHub Actions workflow on the exact candidate revision and inspect the provider result. Demonstrate at least one representative negative canary: temporarily introduce or select a controlled defect that the new test floor is expected to catch, observe the target gate fail for the right reason, then remove/repair the canary and observe the exact final head pass. Do not leave the deliberate defect in the durable branch. If the provider cannot be reached, report the proof ceiling as PROVIDER-RUNTIME BLOCKED instead of calling the workflow green.

9. COMPLEMENT EXISTING PROMPT OWNERS
Use P51 when the immediate need is only exact zero-token local test commands. Use P32 to repair an already failing CI/validation lane. Preserve P11-style canonical validator composition rather than copying validators into workflows. This prompt owns creation/strengthening of the unattended automated-test floor. P105 owns validated promotion after that floor exists; hand off there only when automated push/merge/release/deploy is actually desired.

SECOND PASS
After the first green provider run, inspect the repository and workflow evidence again from the failure side. Ask: what realistic defect could still pass, what healthy state could fail nondeterministically, what required check could silently skip, what event could bypass the workflow, and what duplicated command could drift? Repair concrete findings and rerun affected proof. Do not manufacture changes when this falsification pass finds no practical gap.

DELIVER
Keep the closeout compact and evidence-bearing: detected stack; canonical test command(s); tests/fixtures/harness surfaces added or strengthened; GitHub Actions workflow and triggers; schedule semantics if configured; deterministic controls; negative-canary result; exact-head provider run; skipped/blocked gates; changed files; commit/PR/mainline state; proof ceiling; and the first executable next action. Explain the result in plain language so a novice can tell what now happens automatically while they are away. Do not call test automation complete merely because a workflow file exists.
